a1
Joseph was seventeen. His father Jacob loved him most, and gave him a fine robe.
a2
His brothers hated him. Joseph dreamed that the sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to him.
b1
His father rebuked him, but kept the matter in mind. Then Jacob sent him to his brothers at Dothan.
b2
Here comes that dreamer, they said. Let us kill him and throw him into a pit.
c1
Reuben said: do not take his life. They stripped off his robe, and threw him into an empty pit.
c2
Judah said: let us sell him. Joseph was pulled from the pit and sold to traders for twenty pieces of silver.
d1
The brothers dipped his robe in goat's blood and sent it to Jacob.
d2
Jacob said: a wild beast has devoured my son. He mourned, and refused to be comforted.
e1
In Egypt, Joseph was sold to Potiphar.
h1
The brothers' hatred grew in steps: unkind words, more hatred, then a plot.
h2
Envy rarely begins with a plot. It begins with a closed heart.
h3
Deal with envy while it is small, before it hardens in you.
h4
Today, say one kind word to someone you envy.
i
Whose success is hard for you to celebrate?
